findings.claim: The Lost Boys is described as a Warner Bros. production, and a knowledge check says Warner Bros. produced it.
findings.truth: Richard Donner Production made The Lost Boys; Warner Bros. distributed it.
findings.evidence: The Lost Boys Wikipedia plot and infobox (fetched): production company Richard Donner Production; distributor Warner Bros.

findings.claim: Dracula's 1931 ending is said to satisfy a Production Code demand for moral order.
findings.truth: Dracula predates the Production Code's rigid enforcement, which began in 1934, so its ending cannot be explained as compliance with that requirement.
findings.evidence: Hays Code Wikipedia (fetched), enforcement history: rigid enforcement began in 1934; the 1931 date is confirmed by the specification.

findings.claim: The Lost Boys gang-initiation moment is located on the boardwalk.
findings.truth: After the hideout sequence, the gang takes Michael to a railway bridge, where they hang over the drop.

findings.claim: The Hays Code prevented Pillow Talk from delivering physical intimacy directly.
findings.truth: The Code restricted sexual content; it did not prohibit all physical intimacy.
findings.evidence: Hays Code Wikipedia (fetched), content and enforcement sections.

findings.claim: Ferris commandeers a float in the parade sequence.
findings.truth: Ferris jumps onto a float in an actual parade and lip-syncs to two pop songs.
findings.evidence: Ferris Bueller's Day Off Wikipedia plot and parade-production sections (fetched).

findings.claim: Invasion of the Body Snatchers is described as an Allied Artists production.
findings.truth: Walter Wanger Productions made the independent film; Allied Artists distributed it.
findings.evidence: Invasion of the Body Snatchers Wikipedia infobox and introduction (fetched).

findings.claim: A single comparative-study question is said to carry the largest share of marks in the US-film written paper.
findings.truth: The comparative section has 50 of Component 1's 70 marks and contains two stepped questions plus one comparison question; the specification does not assign that 50-mark total to one question.
findings.evidence: spec 2.1 Assessment, pp. 15–16 equivalent markdown lines 996–1051.

findings.claim: The contextual reason is labelled the AO1 component of the comparative answer.
findings.truth: The comparison question assesses AO2 only. Contextual knowledge should be applied to make the comparison, rather than labelled as the question's AO1 component.

findings.claim: The Hays Code is said to prohibit physical intimacy on screen.
findings.truth: The Code restricted sexual content; it did not prohibit all physical intimacy.
findings.evidence: Hays Code Wikipedia (fetched), content and enforcement sections.

findings.claim: Detailed shot, lighting, editing and sound claims are made for the Dracula staircase and The Lost Boys boardwalk and railway-bridge sequences.
findings.truth: The fetched plot source confirms the railway bridge but not the asserted micro-details. Recheck all scene analysis against a licensed copy of each film; retain only observations that can be verified from the primary film.
findings.evidence: The Lost Boys Wikipedia plot and production sections (fetched); no fetchable primary film source was used for the shot-by-shot claims.

findings.claim: The comparison prompt treats the Singin' in the Rain title number or Good Morning as a solo ballad.
findings.truth: The title number is a solo musical number, not a ballad, and Good Morning is a group number. Either compare musical numbers generally or select genuinely comparable solo ballads; this requires coordinated changes to the prompt and its marking guidance.
findings.evidence: Singin' in the Rain Wikipedia plot and songs sections (fetched).

findings.claim: The lesson calls E.T.'s closet disguise the first-contact scene and builds several analyses on it.
findings.truth: The fetched plot summary places the initial encounter at the garden shed; production notes identify the closet as a later disguise. Rewatch the licensed film and rebuild the affected sequence analysis, examples and questions around one correctly identified scene.
findings.evidence: E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial Wikipedia plot and filming sections (fetched).

findings.claim: The exam tip asserts a board-wide rule for questions worth eight marks or more.
findings.truth: The specification sets Section A's total and assessment objectives but does not establish an eight-mark threshold or the stated rule. Remove or source this claim from current assessment materials before presenting it as examiner practice.
findings.evidence: spec 2.1 Assessment, lines 996–1051; no current examiner-report source fetched.

summary: Six lessons contain verified fixes or items needing adjudication. Thirteen surgical edits correct nine verified findings; four broader or insufficiently sourced concerns are left unedited.
